content.value_statement: Agents often lose useful context across sessions. This skill guides layered memory design with vectors, graphs, and temporal retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Explains working, short-term, long-term, entity, and temporal memory layers.
Compares vector RAG, knowledge graphs, and temporal knowledge graphs.
Shows example patterns for entity tracking and temporal memory queries.
Provides retrieval, consolidation, and memory architecture selection guidance.
Connects memory design with context loading and agent architecture.
limitations: Does not include runnable storage adapters or database setup scripts.
Does not enforce privacy, retention, or consent policies automatically.
Benchmark claims should be verified against current systems before production use.
Requires separate engineering work to implement persistence and retrieval.

use_cases.title: Plan Persistent Agent Memory
use_cases.description: Design memory layers for assistants that need continuity across sessions.

use_cases.title: Model Entity Relationships
use_cases.description: Choose graph-based memory when products, users, or concepts need connected reasoning.

use_cases.title: Define Temporal Retrieval
use_cases.description: Add validity periods so agents can answer questions about changing facts over time.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Memory Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a memory architecture for an agent that must remember user preferences across sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Retrieval Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare vector RAG, knowledge graph memory, and temporal graph memory for my agent use case.

prompt_templates.title: Design Entity Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an entity memory plan for tracking people, organizations, relationships, confidence, and source attribution.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Temporal Graph Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a temporal knowledge graph retrieval strategy with validity periods, consolidation rules, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Design memory for a customer support agent.
output_examples.output: A layered plan with session memory, long-term customer facts, entity relationships, and retention controls.

output_examples.input: Decide whether vector search is enough for relationship questions.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff analysis explaining when vectors work and when graph traversal is required.

output_examples.input: Plan retrieval for facts that change over time.
output_examples.output: A temporal memory approach using validity periods, current-fact filters, and historical lookup behavior.

best_practices: Start with the simplest memory layer that meets query needs.
Store timestamps, source, confidence, and retention rules with important facts.
Test retrieval quality with realistic questions before expanding storage.
anti_patterns: Store every interaction forever without consolidation or retention rules.
Use only vector search when relationship reasoning is required.
Inject large memory dumps into context instead of retrieving targeted facts.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design agent memory layers, retrieval patterns, consolidation rules, and graph-based memory structures.

faq.question: Does it install a memory database?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples, not database installation or runtime adapters.

faq.question: Can it help with temporal knowledge graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains validity periods, temporal retrieval, and handling facts that change over time.

faq.question: Is it suitable for privacy-sensitive systems?
faq.answer: It can guide design, but teams must add consent, retention, access control, and deletion policies.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should I start using it?
faq.answer: Define your queries, entities, retention needs, and acceptable retrieval latency before choosing storage technology.
